correctness.rationale: Stepwise proof: insertion-depth PGF gives exact mean and second moments; conditional parent-centered innovation xi_j has variance v_j; the orthogonal expansion T_n-ET_n=sum_j[1+(n-j)p_j]xi_j yields exact normalized variance. For beta<1, hub probabilities squared are geometrically summable and weighted depth second moments are O(log² j), yielding a convergent nonzero martingale and centered n-scaled L²/a.s. limit; cumulative weight perturbations give absolutely summable mean corrections. For beta>=1, each dyadic arrival assigns uniformly positive conditional mass to two distinct earlier hubs whose expected depths differ uniformly; Jensen then forces a positive contribution to normalized variance at every dyadic time, at least logarithmically many. Exact rational checker passed 1602 assertions; finite checks supplement but do not prove the infinite argument.

originality.rationale: The exact innovation identity is prior work and positive-side convergence may be covered by 2019 profile theory. The novelty assessed is the sharp fixed-family exponent boundary, including a proven log n lower bound for Var(T_n)/n² at every beta>=1, contrasted with a finite positive n² variance coefficient for beta<1. A read of relevant primary literature and six published-finding corpus searches did not identify an implication proving this combined boundary. Search absence is not uniqueness; older weighted-path-length treatments and other general variance lower bounds remain historical risks.

value.rationale: The 2026 motivating work explicitly seeks conditions beyond p_j=O(1/j). Geometrically sparse hubs model a natural borderline between negligible cumulated mass and persistent macroscopic attachment preference. Exact sharp exponent beta=1 separates a finite positive normalized path-length variance with an L² limit from at least logarithmically divergent normalized variance. This is an all-n structural phase boundary for a naturally defined family, not a small numerical increment or the already-known positive-regime convergence result.
